_comment: The editorial half of the pack. No parser can derive what a colour MEANS, what a component is FOR, or what a builder must not do, so those live here by hand and build-pack.mjs merges them with the derived half. Everything not in this file is generated and must not be hand edited.
name: Sample Design System
premise: A small design system that exists to be held to. Two brands, six components, three token tiers, and a set of rules a machine can check. It is deliberately ordinary: the interesting part is not the components, it is that an agent can be told what it may do here and then be checked against it.
north_stars: The design system is a contract, not a suggestion. If a rule cannot be checked it is an intention, and it is labelled as one.
A brand skins at the semantic tier or it does not skin. Anything else is a fork with a nicer name.
A check that did not run is not a check that passed.
The agent is not asked to write good code. It is asked to satisfy a schema, and the schema is this pack.

roles.surface-page: The ground the interface sits on. Never carries content directly.
roles.surface-raised: Anything that sits above the page: cards, inputs, menus.
roles.surface-sunken: A well inside a raised surface, and the resting state of a secondary control.
roles.surface-inverse: The far end of the scale, for the few things that must read as a different layer entirely.
roles.text-primary: Content. The default. Anything a person is meant to read.
roles.text-secondary: Labels and supporting text that is still meant to be read.
roles.text-muted: Text that is present but not addressed to the reader: placeholders, disabled states.
roles.text-inverse: Text on surface-inverse, and nowhere else.
roles.accent-base: Exactly one thing: the action this screen exists for, plus the focus ring. It is not a brand colour to decorate with. The moment it means two things it means nothing.
roles.accent-hover: The same action under a pointer.
roles.accent-subtle: A wash of the accent, for the background of a selected row. Never for text.
roles.accent-contrast: The text colour that is legible on accent-base.
roles.border-subtle: The edge of a surface. Structural, not decorative.
roles.border-strong: The edge of a control a person can act on.
roles.border-focus: Keyboard focus. Always visible, always two pixels, never removed.
roles.status-success: A thing finished and it worked.
roles.status-warning: A thing that needs attention but is not yet wrong.
roles.status-danger: A thing that failed or is about to destroy something.

components.name: DesignSystem
components.purpose: The root every surface sits inside. It picks the brand and supplies the vendor library the structural theme it needs, so those are one decision made once rather than two decisions made in every application. Nothing else in the repository may import the vendor, which is why this is a component rather than a stray provider file.

components.name: Button
components.purpose: The one control that performs an action. Primary is the action the screen exists for, secondary is everything else, and there is at most one primary on a screen.

components.name: Badge
components.purpose: Standing, as a word. Never the only carrier of a state: the badge says the word, the colour agrees with it.

components.name: Card
components.purpose: A raised surface that groups one subject. It has a title and a body and it does not nest inside another card.

components.name: Input
components.purpose: A single line of text from a person, with its label always present and its error message always adjacent. The label is not a placeholder.

components.name: Tabs
components.purpose: One surface, several views of it. Not navigation, and not a wizard: the views are peers and the choice is cheap.

components.name: Toast
components.purpose: A short report that something happened, on the inverse surface so it reads as a different layer. It reports, it never asks.

components.name: Stack
components.purpose: The only way to space things. Layout is a design decision, so it comes from the pack rather than from whatever stylesheet a feature happens to own. Wraps the vendor stack for the flex plumbing and supplies the gap from the token layer. It has no Figma counterpart, because auto layout is already the design tool's answer to the same question.

components.name: Stat
components.purpose: One figure and what it means. The figure is tabular and never reflows as it changes, so a screen full of these is readable at a glance and a screenshot at rest looks like the screen at rest.

components.name: Meter
components.purpose: A proportion, shown as a bar and said as a number. The bar is the quick read and the number is the actual answer, because a bar alone is a shape nobody can quote.

components.name: RecordRow
components.purpose: One line of a record: what it is, how it is doing, and the figure. Built from Badge so standing is said as a word here too, rather than as a colour this row invented.

rules: Every value in a stylesheet is a var(--ds-*). A raw colour, length or duration the token layer already carries is a bug. If the layer is missing something, add it to the layer.
At most one accented action per screen. The accent means the action this screen exists for, and the focus ring. Nothing else.
Anything said with colour is also said with a word. Colour is never the only carrier of a state.
Every actionable control is at least 44 pixels effective, and keyboard focus is always visible at two pixels in the focus colour.
Figures are tabular and do not reflow as they change. A screenshot at rest looks identical to the interface at rest.
Honour prefers-reduced-motion. Durations collapse and the state change still happens.
Only the components in this pack may be used. A design that needs something else is a request to add it here, not a local component in a feature folder.
Every change ships behind a flag that is off. Merging is not releasing.

refuses.says: No raw hex, rgb, or pixel value in a component where a token exists.
No component imported from outside this pack.
The accent colour is not used for decoration, headers, or borders that are not focus.
A brand may not set a component-tier token, and may not omit a semantic key another brand has.
A component that animates carries a prefers-reduced-motion guard in the same stylesheet.
A state is never carried by colour alone.

visual._comment: Fraction of pixels allowed to differ between a story screenshot and the Figma frame export before the visual check comments on the pull request. Advisory in v1, see docs/DECISIONS.md.

contrast._comment: Every pairing the system actually puts on screen, and the ratio it must clear. The build computes these from each brand and refuses to compile a brand that fails one, so an illegal palette is a broken build rather than an accessibility finding six months later. Text needs 4.5 to 1 and anything structural needs 3 to 1, per WCAG 2.2 AA.

vendor._comment: The component library underneath the pack. Its runtime --bs-* custom properties are driven by this system's semantic tier, so switching brand re-skins every vendor component with no rebuild. The map below is compiled to design-system/tokens.vendor.css by build-pack.mjs and must not be hand maintained. An entry whose right side is not a semantic token stops the build.
